script.spoken: Antarctica holds 61% of Earth's fresh water. It's locked in ice over 2 kilometres thick. Now imagine that ice sheet melting. By 2100, Antarctic losses alone may add around 11 centimetres to sea level. The West Antarctic sheet alone could add 3.3 metres. But losing it would take 2,000 to 13,000 years. So the danger is a slow, unstoppable rise, not a sudden flood.
